{{Nihongo|'''Yamaha Corporation'''|ヤマハ株式会社|Yamaha [[Kabushiki gaisha]]|{{IPAc-en|ˈ|j|ɑː|m|ə|h|ɑː}}; {{IPA|ja|jamaha}}}} is a Japanese multinational musical instrument and audio equipment manufacturer.

It is one of the constituents of [[Nikkei 225]] and is the world's largest musical instrument manufacturing company.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Fosler-Lussier |first1=Danielle |title=Music on the Move |date=2020 |publisher=University of Michigan Press |page=123}}</ref>

The former [[motorcycle]] division was established in 1955 as [[Yamaha Motor Company|Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd.]], which started as an affiliated company but has been spun-off as its own independent company.

== History ==
[[File:Torakusu-yamaha.jpg|thumb|[[Torakusu Yamaha]], founder of Yamaha Corporation]]

{{Nihongo|'''Nippon Gakki Co., Ltd.'''|日本楽器製造株式会社|Nihon Gakki Seizō [[Kabushiki gaisha]]|{{literal translation|Japan Musical Instrument Manufacture}}}} was established in 1887 as a [[reed organ]] manufacturer by [[Torakusu Yamaha]] ({{Lang|ja|山葉寅楠}}) in [[Hamamatsu]], Shizuoka Prefecture, and was incorporated on 12 October 1897. In 1900, the company manufactured the first piano to be made in Japan,<ref name=":0" /> and its first grand piano two years later. In 1987, 100 years after the first reed organ built by Yamaha, the company was renamed Yamaha Corporation in honor of its founder.<ref name="Lenhoff">{{cite book |last1=Lenhoff |first1=Alan |last2=Robertson |first2=David |title=Classic Keys: Keyboard sounds that launched rock music |date=2019 |publisher=University of North Texas Press |location=Denton, Texas, USA |isbn=9781574417760|page=337}}</ref> The company's origins as a [[musical instrument]] [[manufacturer]] are still reflected today in the group's logo—a trio of interlocking [[tuning fork]]s.<ref name=brand>{{cite web |title=Yamaha Corporate Information |url=http://www.global.yamaha.com/about/brand/index.html |website=Yamaha Global |publisher=Yamaha Corporation |access-date=31 December 2006 |archive-date=12 December 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061212215032/http://www.global.yamaha.com/about/brand/index.html |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.yamaha.com/en/about/history/|title=Brand and History - About Us - Yamaha Corporation|website=Yamaha.com|publisher=Yamaha|language=en-US|access-date=1 July 2018}}</ref>

After [[World War II]], company president <!-- Tomiko -->[[Genichi Kawakami]] repurposed the remains of the company's war-time production machinery and the company's expertise in metallurgical technologies to the manufacture of [[motorcycle]]s. [[Yamaha YA-1|The YA-1 (AKA Akatombo, the "Red Dragonfly")]], of which 125 were built in the first year of production (1954), was named in honour of the founder. It was a 125cc, single [[cylinder (engine)|cylinder]], two-stroke street bike patterned after the German [[DKW RT 125]] (which the British munitions firm, [[Birmingham Small Arms Company|BSA]], had also copied in the post-war era and manufactured as the [[BSA Bantam|Bantam]] and [[Harley-Davidson]] as the [[Harley-Davidson Hummer|Hummer]]). In 1955,<ref name=forbes>{{cite web |title=Yamaha Motor |url=https://www.forbes.com/companies/yamaha-motor/ |work=Forbes Global 2000 List}}</ref> the success of the YA-1 resulted in the founding of [[Yamaha Motor Company|Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd.]], splitting the motorcycle division from the company. Also, in 1954 the [[Yamaha Music School]] was founded.<ref name=":0" />

Yamaha has grown into the world's largest manufacturer of musical instruments (including pianos, [[Silent piano|"silent" pianos]], [[drum]]s, [[guitar]]s, [[brass instruments]], [[woodwind]]s, [[violin]]s, [[viola]]s, [[cello|cellos]], and [[vibraphone]]s), and a leading manufacturer of [[semiconductor]]s, [[Audio-visual|audio/visual]], computer-related products, sporting goods, [[home appliance]]s, specialty [[metals]], and [[industrial robot]]s.<ref name=usaci>{{cite web |title=Yamaha Corporate History |url=http://usa.yamaha.com/about_yamaha/corporate_information/ |publisher=Yamaha Corporation of America & Yamaha Corporation |access-date=26 April 2011}}</ref> Yamaha released the [[Yamaha CS-80]] in 1977.

In 1983, Yamaha made the first commercially successful digital synthesizer, the [[Yamaha DX7]].

In 1988, Yamaha shipped the world's first [[CD-R|CD recorder]].<ref>{{cite magazine|last1=Verna|first1=Paul|title=CD-R Enjoys Massive Growth In A Wide Range Of Markets|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=SQ0EAAAAMBAJ&q=%22first+CD+recorder%22+yamaha&pg=PA52|access-date=21 March 2018|magazine=Billboard|date=3 April 1999}}</ref> Yamaha purchased [[Sequential Circuits]] in 1988.<ref name=sos99march>

==Business segments==
Yamaha is segmented into three primary business domains of musical instruments, audio equipment, and others (industrial machinery and components, etc.)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.yamaha.com/en/about/pdf/corporate_profile_2023_en.pdf|title=Yamaha Corporate Profile 2023|date=2023|publisher=Yamaha Corporate Communications Division|access-date=9 August 2024|archive-date=7 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240807044145/https://www.yamaha.com/en/about/pdf/corporate_profile_2023_en.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

* Musical Instruments – the manufacture and sales of pianos; digital musical instruments; brass, woodwind, string, and percussion instruments; and other music-related activities.
** Pianos and [[Celesta]]s
** Digital Musical Instruments
** Brass and Woodwinds, Strings/Percussion
** Guitars
* Audio Equipment – the manufacture and sales of audio products, professional audio equipment, information and telecommunication equipment, and certain other products.
** Consumer
*** Yamaha Home Audio
** B2B
*** [[Yamaha Pro Audio]]
*** Yamaha Unified Communications, Inc.

* Industrial Machinery and Components (IMC) & others – electronic devices business, automobile interior wood components, factory automation (FA) equipment, golf products and a resort business.

=== Living room business ===
The company began by manufacturing high-end furniture based on its expertise in wood processing for piano manufacturing, and was spun off into a separate company in 1991 with the establishment of YAMAHA Livingtec (YLT). The company manufactured and sold [[unit bath]]s, [[system kitchen]]s, and other products. In 1992, the company decided to stop selling system furniture, and after narrowing down its product lineup, it terminated orders and production in March 2005.<ref name="furniture">[https://www.yamaha-living.co.jp/news/20041224/index.html Notice Regarding Discontinuation of Production of Yamaha Furniture Products] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107101606/http://www.yamaha-living.co.jp/news/20041224/index.html |date=7 November 2012 }}(24 December 2004, Yamaha Livingtec News Release)</ref>

In 2010, Yamaha sold its 85.1% stake in YLT to [[Japan Industrial Partners]] and three foreign investment funds as part of a restructuring. At this point, the YAMAHA brand and company name continued, but the company essentially withdrew from management. Subsequently, YLT conducted a [[management buyout|MBO]] of the investments of Yamaha and the investment funds, and the company name was changed as of 1 October 2013<ref name="mbo">[https://www.yamaha-living.co.jp/news/20130628/index.html Notice of Capital Structure and Trade Name Change] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130915053345/http://www.yamaha-living.co.jp/news/20130628/index.html |date=15 September 2013 }}(28 June 2013, Yamaha Livingtec News Release)</ref><ref name="mbo_nikkei">[https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXNASDD280I0_Y3A620C1TJ1000/ Yamaha Livingtec MBOs under the name Toklas] (28 June 2013, Nihon Keizai Shimbun)</ref> and withdrew from the housing equipment business in both name and reality.

==Corporate mission==
{{Nihongo|''Kandō''|感動}} is a Japanese word used by Yamaha Corporation to describe its corporate mission. {{Lang|ja-latn|Kandō}} is the sensation of profound excitement and gratification derived from experiencing supreme quality and performance.<ref name=ymukmission>{{cite web
 | title     = Yamaha Corporate Mission
 | url     = http://www.yamaha-motor.eu/uk/corporate/mission.aspx
 | publisher     = Yamaha Motor UK
 | access-date     = 25 May 2015
 | archive-date     = 25 May 2015
 | archive-url     = https://web.archive.org/web/20150525161431/http://www.yamaha-motor.eu/uk/corporate/mission.aspx
 | url-status     = dead
 }}</ref> Some reasonable English equivalents are "emotionally touching" or "emotionally moving".

== Yamaha Music Foundation ==
{{Main|Yamaha Music Foundation}}
Yamaha Corporation is widely known for its music teaching program that began in 1954. In a continuation of that program, the Yamaha Music Foundation was established by the authority of the Japanese Ministry of Education for the purpose of promoting music education and music popularization In 1966.<ref>{{cite web |title=Yamaha Music Foundation History |url=http://www.yamaha-mf.or.jp/english/about/history.html |publisher=Yamaha Music Foundation }}</ref>

Yamaha Corporation (ヤマハ株式会社, Yamaha Kabushiki gaisha; ; Japanese pronunciation: [jamaha]) is a Japanese multinational musical instrument and audio equipment manufacturer.
It is one of the constituents of Nikkei 225 and is the world's largest musical instrument manufacturing company.
The former motorcycle division was established in 1955 as Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd., which started as an affiliated company but has been spun-off as its own independent company.
